Senses.Explanation: That side, the other side, or beyond: a relational expression built from 'that bank or side' (那畔). The allowlisted record has 866 occurrences in 233 storage files. The deictic contrast is explicit. Faxi Yin asks about 'the matter on that side' (那畔事) and then 'the matter on this side' (者邊事). In another public exchange, an unnamed monk says that as soon as words are involved one falls on 'this side' (遮畔), then asks Shending Yunwai Ze for news from 'that side' (那畔底消息). The word builds noun phrases for a matter, person, saying, road, or news located there. Its most frequent fixed expansion is 'beyond Awesome Sound' (威音那畔), a locative formula used in addresses and verses. Yuanjie Ying speaks of 'one saying from beyond Awesome Sound' (威音那畔一句); Cishou Huaishen asks 'what is the road on that side?' (如何是那畔路). Zen thus bends an ordinary demonstrative into a productive way of marking what a teaching-seat question places beyond the present side, while the exact referent remains deliberately supplied by each surrounding exchange. Yinyuan Longqi places the direct-teaching gateway on the far side of Awesome Sound; Yuanwu Keqin asks who can distinguish its clue. These extend the same relational ‘far side’ into lineage address without making it a second place.
Senses.Note: Corpus counts: 866 hits in 233 storage files. The Awesome-Sound expansion has 470 hits in 173 files; 'the matter on that side,' 41/29; 'a person on that side,' 10/7; 'a saying on that side,' 4/3; and direct 'what is that side?' constructions, 5/5. Standard self-definition searches returned no Chinese Chan equation. Their zero results and excluded non-Chinese evidence are preserved in WORK rather than printed as unattested quotations.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanjie Ying (元潔瑩禪師語錄), in Yuanjie Ying's opening hall address at Ancient Dongshan Anou Chan Monastery. Yuanjie Ying is the exact speaker who says that a phrase from beyond Awesome Sound encompasses the whole and that the complete body appears with not a mote established. Dongshan in the venue heading names the monastery; it does not make Dongshan Liangjie the speaker of this address.
